definitions.explanation: A general term for any machine capable of flight, including airplanes, helicopters, and other flying vehicles. A formal and technical term compared to the everyday 飛行機.

examples.japanese: {航空機|こうくうき}の{部品|ぶひん}を{製造|せいぞう}する{工場|こうじょう}。
examples.english: A factory that manufactures aircraft parts.

examples.japanese: {小型|こがた}{航空機|こうくうき}が{緊急|きんきゅう}{着陸|ちゃくりく}した。
examples.english: A small aircraft made an emergency landing.

examples.japanese: この{空港|くうこう}では{一日|いちにち}に{数百|すうひゃく}{機|き}の{航空機|こうくうき}が{離着陸|りちゃくりく}している。
examples.english: Several hundred aircraft take off and land at this airport every day.

notes:
A formal, inclusive term for any flying machine. Broader than {飛行機|ひこうき} (airplane), which refers specifically to fixed-wing aircraft.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {航空機|こうくうき}{産業|さんぎょう} (aircraft industry)
- {航空機|こうくうき}{事故|じこ} (aircraft accident)
- {小型|こがた}{航空機|こうくうき} (small aircraft)
- {無人|むじん}{航空機|こうくうき} (unmanned aircraft, drone)

SCOPE NOTE:
{航空機|こうくうき} covers all aircraft including helicopters, gliders, and drones, while {飛行機|ひこうき} typically refers only to fixed-wing airplanes. In everyday conversation, {飛行機|ひこうき} is far more common; {航空機|こうくうき} is preferred in news reports, technical writing, and official documents.

COUNTER: {機|き}
